newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: C-C Amatil shares dumped on downgrade.
newsitem.headline: C-C Amatil shares dumped on downgrade.

text.p: Shares in beverage bottler Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd slumped in early trade on Thursday, losing 6.4 percent to an intraday low of A$15.25 with brokers citing a downgrade by investment bank Merrill Lynch for the soft performance.
"It's fallen this morning on the back of the downgrade by Merrill's," said a Sydney-based broker.
While others concurred, they noted the volatility of the growth-oriented stock in trending markets.
"Obviously the downgrading didn't help it at all, but when the market comes off reasonably heavily, Coke seems to be one of the first to cop it," said Reynolds and Co dealer, Peter Struk.
C-C Amatil recently finalised a A$3.4 billion deal with Philippines-based beverage group San Miguel Corp to create the largest Coca-Cola bottler outside the U.S..

Under the share swap deal, which saw plenty of discussions over San Miguel's representation on the board, C-C Amatil acquires San Miguel's soft drink subsidiary while San miguel receives 192.5 million shares or about 25 percent of C-C Amatil. At the time analysts saw the deal as boosting C-C Amatil, given
that the Filipino bottler was earning almost identical profits to C-C Amatil but on half the sales.
The Coca-Cola Co owns about 33 percent of C-C Amatil.
By 11.50 a.m. (0150 GMT), C-C Amatil shares had regained some ground to be 95 cents down at A$15.35.
